instruction: Retail shell with back rooms. Open `/opt/blender/blender` first; Bonsai is available inside it as the installed BIM extension. The Desktop contains an editable IFC4 seed file at /home/user/Desktop/init.ifc. Open that seed project in Bonsai with the IFC project open controls and inspect it as needed. The seed contains placeholder space names and no final window objects. In Bonsai/Blender, rename the spaces and add the required window objects, then save the only required deliverable as /home/user/Desktop/result.ifc using Bonsai's IFC save/export controls. The saved IFC must contain exactly three real IfcSpace objects with these exact names: Sales, Storage, and WC. Storage is the back-room storage area. Model the building as a rectangular single-storey shell about 10 m by 6 m with walls about 3.0 m high and one floor slab. Include at least 6 wall-like IfcWall or IfcWallStandardCase elements, at least 1 IfcSlab, at least 3 IfcDoor elements, and at least 3 IfcWindow elements. Create real IFC/BIM elements rather than ordinary Blender mesh placeholders or visual-only geometry. The exported IFC should use the IFC4 schema and have unique GlobalId values for IfcRoot objects. The shaped model should have an overall size roughly matching the shell, with X span about 10 m, Y span about 6 m, and Z span about 3.0 m. Other coordinates, wall thicknesses, opening positions, materials, object type names, relationship nesting, property sets, and harmless exporter metadata may vary as long as the saved IFC satisfies these requirements.
